title: Card deposit
context: Users top up their trading account by card. The deposit must be saved and the card charged together; the author added @Transactional to make it atomic.

refs.title: Spring transaction management: @Transactional in depth (Marco Behler)
What is Spring Framework? Proxies and AOP (Marco Behler)

points.title: @Transactional bypassed by self-invocation
points.why: Spring applies transactions through a proxy. Calling saveAndCharge from inside the same class skips the proxy, so no transaction is started.
points.fix: Put @Transactional on the public entry point, or move saveAndCharge into another bean.

points.title: Card charged inside a DB transaction
points.why: The DB connection stays open during a slow HTTP call. If the commit fails after the charge, the customer is charged with no deposit recorded. A rollback can't undo a card payment.
points.fix: Save the deposit as PENDING and commit, then charge, then mark it CREDITED (or use an outbox or saga with compensation).

points.title: No idempotency
points.why: A client retry or a double tap creates a second deposit and charges the card twice.
points.fix: Require an idempotency key on the request, store it with a unique constraint, and pass it to the payment provider.

points.title: Request not validated

why.java: Null user ids and zero or negative amounts reach the payment provider.
why.kotlin: Zero or negative amounts (and amounts above the deposit limit) reach the payment provider.

points.fix: Validate the request with @Valid and bean validation, and check the amount is positive and within limits.
